AUTO-007.summary: Owner-accepted clarification on 14 October 2026: the former unconditional transport retry promise applies only to failures known safe to retry. Uncertain SendGrid submissions retain visible Unknown action/run states and error details, with no automatic or manual resend. Existing safe retries retain their absolute 1, 5, 15, 30 and 60 minute offsets and action keys. Local action keys do not establish SendGrid idempotency; no reconciliation or exactly-once capability is claimed. See docs/launch-runtime.md#uncertain-delivery-contract--14-october-2026.

AUTO-009.summary: Clarifies the AUTO-007 uncertain-outcome exception: manual retry accepts only Failed runs, creates a linked retryOf run and retains original evidence and completed actions. Unknown runs cannot be manually resent; this adds no reconciliation operation or provider-side idempotency guarantee.

NOTIFY-003.summary: Clarifies that delivery retries follow AUTO-007's safe-retry requirement. Uncertain submission remains visibly Unknown instead of being converted to a confirmed failure eligible for resend. SendGrid acceptance is not proof of mailbox delivery; the in-app notification remains available. No new provider, authority or migration is introduced.

HOME-002.summary: Supersedes HOME-001. The owner identity plate is replaced by a public product landing page at `/` with a hero of data streaming into one Projects screen, illustrated sections for tables, views, safe schema changes, the practical parts (CSV, automations, read-only AI) and ownership, and a closing call to action. Retained: no record content or public views, a link to `/signin`, the configurable credit to runeditrun.com with no telemetry or phone-home, and config-driven product and workspace names. Superseded: the former ban on a feature tour. Still excluded: pricing, testimonials, metrics and integrations the product does not ship. No new sessionless path or data change. See docs/contract-transition.md#public-product-landing--8-october-2026. Amended 12 October 2026 with DOCS-001: the landing and the docs share one header and footer; the header links Docs, the source repository and Sign in; the hero and closing call to action link to the docs, at least two sections link to the guide page on their subject, and the footer adds Docs, Source, Sign in and an MIT licence link. Nothing the clause required is removed; the new links are same-site or plain outbound anchors, so the page still loads nothing from another origin and gains no sessionless path.

DOCS-001.summary: New clause. Every page in docs/site.json is served without a session at /docs and /docs/<slug> inside the same header and footer as the landing, each page links to its source on GitHub, an unlisted slug is a genuine 404 and no third-party resource loads. The docs routes and their /docs and /docs/ public paths already existed; this records them as a guaranteed, tested surface. package.json now names the public repository so the Edit this page links and repository links in the pages are built. No data or migration change.

AUTH-BASE-001.summary: Standalone local sign-in uses the checkout key and real Base dev sessions; the captured-mail sender and inbox page are retired. Hosted /signin names incomplete owner claim and missing or failed email configuration without claiming a request was received. Mail tests retain doubles only at their provider edge. Demo files and host remain owned by the demo lane.

RECORDS-004.summary: Launch readiness opens its included base without creating a duplicate; manual templates retain preview and adoption. View CSV checkbox values use Yes/No, accepted by the existing importer.

RECORDS-007.summary: Agent-proposed schema changes: an owner-issued proposing key (one base, 30-day maximum, revocable, digest only) reaches only the proposal door over REST and MCP, proposes schema, views and forms with an impact preview, and cannot adopt, read records or manage keys. Only the owner adopts through release.adopt with the existing recheck; proposal text is inert. No existing clause is weakened.

HOME-003.summary: The installed Lobby and public setup state read Base’s durable owner claim, independently of workspace first-run details. A healthy rer deploy therefore offers Sign in immediately after owner claim, with no setup-token instruction. Signed-in app access still requires the owner to confirm workspace details under SET-003; public disclosure remains limited to claim state and the workspace name.

OPS-002.summary: 15 October 2026: the installation owner can hand ownership to another active member (`member.transfer-ownership`) after a fresh Base email-link proof (`owner:transfer`) in the same session; the new owner receives the owner's exact app scopes, the installation-owner flag and the Base owner role, and Records base schema control. In the same commit the former owner becomes a Base admin, so exactly one owner remains; they keep their app access until they remove themselves through the unchanged removal rules (no owned active campaign, no unresolved assigned decision). The current owner can never be removed, by themselves or anyone else: they hand over first, so the installation always keeps an active owner. Previously the sole owner could never be removed. Security: the step-up proof and actor/target versions are rechecked inside the admission transaction; both people's older sessions end because Base bumps their operator version on a role change; proposing keys issued by the former owner stop working.

VIEW-007.summary: 15 October 2026: launch collections (campaign grid, decision queue, lens list, launch reader) page with a keyset cursor over the requested sort and the record ID instead of a numeric offset, so records added or removed between pages neither repeat nor skip others. Cursor strings from earlier pages are not accepted; clients restart from the first page.

VIEW-005.summary: Global search includes every authorized base, with current row and field checks and canonical record detail links. Launch archive filtering is retained; inaccessible fields never produce matches.

RECORDS-006.summary: Settings prepares and downloads a verified installation .rer archive using the maintained CLI portability format and privacy policy. Only the current installation owner has this door; credentials and private connections remain excluded, and source is kept separately.

VIEW-016.summary: Completes find navigation over all current record view displays. The selected readable cell is highlighted and scrolled into view across pages; calendar/timeline/agenda render their selected fields. A 5,000-order emitted-Worker journey covers desktop and phone. No authority, data model or contract guarantee changes.

VIEW-014.summary: Completes live multi-user record editing and scoped presence. Native browser sessions refresh committed data within two seconds, keep open drafts on their original versions and receive current readable values on stale-write refusals, including final SQL guard races. Presence stores short-lived session handles only, rechecks current policy and native sessions, and never transfers in archives.

migrations.buyerSteps: Apply in the core group before the updates group, preserving all applied SQL. It adds launch dispatch, retry, action-effect, automation-authority and model-call bookkeeping and marks every existing launch event as already dispatched, so no historical mutation replays. Records and authority are unchanged.

Apply in the updates group, preserving all applied SQL. It adds Base provider setup controls; an absent setting means off, so identity-provider sign-in stays off after upgrade until the owner turns it on.

Apply after 9025 in the updates group, preserving all applied SQL. It adds proposing-key bindings and stored agent proposals; existing records, views, forms, keys, grants and memberships are unchanged. Installation archives never carry proposing-key bindings.
Apply after 9026. Additive Base import-kit fences for reversal; existing imports and records are unchanged.

Apply after 9027. Adds the append-only import retirement and erasure journal (its rows cannot be updated or deleted) and refreshes one stream-revision trigger. Existing imports and records are unchanged.

Apply after 9028. Adds a unique index so each execution attempt holds at most one human-evidence resolution. An installation that already holds two for one attempt fails this step: resolve the duplicate before upgrading.

Apply after 9029 in the updates group, preserving all applied SQL. It rewrites only the seven sample-fixture IDs outside the ULID alphabet (two lenses, four automations, one notification read) and every column that references them, so adopted legacy samples accept typed commands. No other row changes; historical receipt JSON keeps the old literal.

Apply after 9030 in the updates group, preserving all applied SQL. It adds two triggers on oa_operators that refuse (last_owner) deactivating, demoting or deleting the Base operator of the active installation owner unless another active principal is already the installation owner in the same transaction. No rows change; hand ownership over with member.transfer-ownership.

Apply after 9031 in the updates group without changing any prior SQL. This adds versioned owner-approved accounting contact, account and tax mappings. It grants no provider access and does not create a payable.

Apply after 9032 in the updates group without changing existing accounts or sessions. This adds optional Base identity-provider link and OIDC transaction storage. A new installation keeps provider sign-in off until configured and approved. Configure IDENTITY_PROVIDER through setup and manage enable, disable or unlink at /auth/settings/identity.

Apply after 9033, preserving all previous migration bytes. This adds Base’s single-use, expiring owner sign-in grant table. Run rer install with the pinned rer (0.2.23) and redeploy before using rer signin.
Apply after 9034. Changes only retained Launch display labels and declared primary fields; record IDs, values and authority remain unchanged.
Apply after 9035. Adds Base import-kit preparation checkpoints for imports prepared across requests; erasure, cancellation and header retirement read them. Additive; kept in archives.
Apply after 9036. Records the source digest a prepared import stream began with, so only the same upload replays under its operation key. Additive.

Apply the additive core migration without changing prior SQL. It stores short-lived presence handles and clears them on removal/erasure; installation archives exclude this transient table. Existing record data and grants stay intact.

agentUpdateInstructions: Upgrade from 0.1.0 by merging this release into your checkout, keeping your customisations and every applied migration byte. Before pulling, stop rer dev and take an export with rer export. Run rer install with the pinned @runeditrun/rer 0.2.50, then rer dev (local) or rer deploy (hosted); both apply the additive migrations listed here in order: core 1220, then updates 9026 to 9037. Hosted mail: set MAIL_PROVIDER to rer (Managed hosting: MAIL_RELAY_URL and MAIL_API_KEY come from RER), sendgrid or resend (MAIL_PROVIDER_API_KEY), plus MAIL_FROM; a hosted installation without one of these refuses email sign-in with a plain message. Local sign-in now uses the checkout key through rer dev; the development outbox page is gone and local mail is never shown in a page. rer deploy claims the owner itself; SETUP_TOKEN is retired at the claim and the Lobby offers Sign in before workspace setup is completed (HOME-003). Launch collection cursors are keysets (VIEW-007): a client holding an offset cursor from 0.1.0 restarts from the first page. The installation owner can hand ownership to another active member (OPS-002) and can no longer be removed; migration 9031 enforces this in the database. Identity-provider sign-in (9026, 9033) stays off until the owner configures and approves it. Settings prepares the installation .rer archive for the owner only (RECORDS-006); credentials, sessions and private connections stay excluded. Keep new providers, scopes and grants inactive until explicitly authorized. Local checks do not establish hosted readiness or full flagship acceptance (ACCEPTANCE.md). Apply core 1250 for live presence. Live views need no provider account or additional configuration.
publicReleaseNotes:
Cradle 0.2.0 sends Managed hosting mail through the RER relay, so a Managed installation needs no SendGrid or Resend account; own-account hosting keeps SendGrid and Resend. A valid login_hint prefills the sign-in email without submitting it.

The launch template becomes a working app: CSV import with review, CSV export of the grid, lenses and decision queue, custom fields, bulk edit with undo, sample data install and removal, durable automations with safe retries, and ownership handover. Records gain reviewed CSV-set and native JSON base imports, portable base exits, an owner-only installation archive in Settings, and agent-proposed schema changes the owner adopts.

rer deploy claims the owner; the Lobby offers Sign in straight away. Local sign-in uses the checkout key; there is no mail outbox page. Documentation is served at /docs.

Migrations 1220 and 9026 to 9037 are additive. Launch paging cursors changed to keysets, so older cursors restart from the first page.

Upgrading a local install: stop dev, rer export, pull, then rer install and rer dev.

Screenshot: .github/assets/release/cradle-0.2.0-records-1440.png (Records at 1440 px: the Project tracker template's Projects grid in local dev).

Local and CI verification only; this release does not claim hosted capacity, live mailbox delivery or full flagship acceptance.
